info.title: Blustone Replica HTTP API
info.description:
# Purpose
Local compatibility-server contract generated from the recovered Blustone 2.8.0.1 ARM native library.

# Evidence status
Route literals are recovered evidence. Most payload/response shapes remain hypotheses until captured from an ARM-capable runtime. Every recovered operation carries `x-reverse-engineering-status` and `x-runtime-confidence` extensions.

# Security status
The APK contains a native shared-secret exchange and request protection layer. The local server implements the recovered P-384/AES-256-CBC/HMAC-SHA384 exchange for emulator compatibility, but it remains a local research server and must not be exposed to the public internet.

# Local workflow
Start locally, point the APK or an ARM test device at the advertised base URL, capture the first request/response pair, then replace the corresponding mock operation with a schema-backed handler.

get.summary: Return the native CDN resource manifest
get.description:
The launcher/CDN layer requests this plain-text manifest before downloading patch packages.

The first three lines are the manifest stamp, package count, and total package bytes. Each following line is `name,stamp,size,step,sign,md5`. Every line must end with a newline.

The client generates `/{name}_{stamp}.pkg` itself. The sixth column is an optional uppercase MD5 of that entire downloaded container, checked by CPVCDN::UnpackAsynTask before unpacking. It is not a URL or filename. The replica emits a separate fifth-column signature for the inner JET; its complete native semantics remain under investigation.

This route is intentionally documented as a compatibility protocol rather than a JSON API.

get.description:
Serves a local `.jet` package after the native client accepts the resource manifest.

The replica only serves explicitly configured package names from `BLUSTONE_PACKAGE_DIR`; path traversal and arbitrary filesystem reads are rejected.

The same handler also accepts `/cdn/{package}.jet`, `/resource/{package}.jet`, and `/resources/{package}.jet` for clients whose recovered URL template includes a prefix. The native downloader’s observed URL is `/{name}_{stamp}.pkg`; the local server maps that allowlisted package URL to the recovered `.jet` bytes and honors HTTP Range requests.

get.summary: Download a native CDN package with Range support
get.description:
This is the URL shape observed after the native client accepts a resource row: `/{name}_{stamp}.pkg`.

The local replica maps the allowlisted package name to the recovered local resource payload and honors the client’s HTTP Range requests.

With BLUSTONE_PACKAGE_MODE=pkgi1, responses contain a reconstructed binary container: a 20-byte header, then records consisting of u8 filename byte length, UTF-8 filename, u32 little-endian payload size, and u32 little-endian absolute payload offset. The header begins with a u64 little-endian stamp and has the item count at offset 16; offsets 8 and 12 remain incompletely understood. Payloads follow the record table. Native unpack completion is not yet verified.

post.summary: Register or retrieve a local guest account
post.description: Creates or retrieves a guest account by device_id, binds the confirmed pvid to the PV-AccessToken transport session, and returns the native login-shaped payload. Observed native form fields: app_code, app_ver, device_id, extra_data, market, platform, srv_id. Native clients encrypt this form after the P-384 exchange. The response contains nonempty otp, stable vs_token, sns_list, begin_utc, and server_url; CPVDataMgr::ParseLoginResult returns early on empty otp and leaves the gameplay host empty. Subsequent native requests use otp in the encrypted form body. Configure BLUSTONE_STATE_FILE to persist accounts, credentials, and transport-session bindings atomically across restarts. This single-process research store is not a production authentication service.

post.description: CSRSyncTutorial::RequestClear posts unsigned type and step with account fields. ReqClearCB reads numeric ret_data.type and ret_data.step and marks that exact pair state3. The replica validates uint32 keys, persists account-scoped completion and acknowledges the same pair on retries. Login and lobby merge stored completion with bootstrap bypass rows, emitting one row per pair with completed truth taking precedence: native Parse can overwrite state3 with a later false row. Ordinary pairs omit unknown rewards. Guided37/1 requires completed37/0, a completed winning local Search and enough owned unlocked traces for the current target. It uses the published local trace exchange threshold to award one full card collection and consume_result.item delta, persisting hunter, trace debit and completed pair together. Repeated acknowledgement omits reward/debit. Original guided reward economics remain unknown; no automatic flag clear or live grant occurs. Native guided recruitment display still requires runtime validation.

post.description: CSRSyncCard::RequestSkillUp posts target_inst_id and skill_idx (type1..5). ReqSkillUpCB reads DIRECT ret_data.target_inst with inst_id and selected skill_N_level:{prev,cur}, plus ret_data.skill_idx, user.gold:{prev,cur} and consumed_inst_list. The replica validates ownership, unlocked slot, reference rank eligibility, role/rank cap and gold before persisting one level and gold together. Inventory lock prevents destruction, not skill improvement. Local policy is +1 per accepted request, gold100*destinationLevel, zero materials; original prices and increment implementation are missing. Each accepted call is a separate upgrade: the native request has no nonce or expected level, so transport exactly-once is not promised. Local refusal code2001 skips native mutation parsing. The separately documented MultiSkillUp route has a different batch response contract.

post.summary: Advance a hunter with credited same-grade materials
post.description: Recovered request posts target_inst_id, source_inst_list as JSON numeric-ID array, and is_tuto0/1. ReqRankUpCB reads user.gold prev/cur and user.deck, then card.target_inst inst_id/rank/rank_up_cnt/exp prev/cur pairs. card.removed_inst_list contains BARE numeric IDs, unlike LevelUp object rows. The inferred revival policy requires ordinary max level, ranks1..4, same-grade unlocked unused materials and capacity=current rank: partial p+n retains rank/EXP; reaching capacity promotes one grade, resets counter and EXP. Overflow refuses. Counts follow historical community guidance;1000 gold/source and5percent bonus per credited material are fixtures. Native skips real source IDs below capacity as synthetic credits, so the server refuses that legacy compatibility edge without renumbering ownership. Target-in-active-battle, protected leader/deck/battle materials and malformed requests refuse atomically. Source consumption prevents retry duplication. Target skills are preserved because this callback does not read automatic unlock fields; new eligible zero-level slots need further investigation. Gold, target, sources, deck cleanup and book maximum persist together. Awakening, guild discounts and original partial/EXP behavior remain unreconstructed. Native preview/partial/full/relaunch validation is pending.

post.summary: Read resource, capsule and hunter trace references
post.description: Native item reference is ret_data{item,trace,global_item}; item.effect is a STRING. Hunter trace use_type3/effect005 or006 binds explicit local item IDs to Gerard/Sylvester. Flat trace rows use item_id/order/type3/source_id n_01_07/thumb_id; native activation requires actual stars on that source. Trace IDs, thresholds and association are local navigation fixtures; no rewards, recruitment or grants are implemented. Local local_ap/use_type1 provides10 AP and local_bp/use_type2 provides5 BP; thumbnails IT_ST/IT_LT are reconstructed candidates. Global prices publish exact buy counts1..3 for Manda5/type1 and gold100/type2; missing native tiers return0, never cap-to-last. Buy request requires target_ref_id, price_type, item_inst_id0, qty1. Unsupported tickets/items/quantities refuse with provisional code2001. Local policy allows3 purchases per resource shared across currencies per UTCday; rollback never reopens a capped cycle, overflow is preserved, and Manda total is charged once free-first. Identity, prices, amount, reset and limit policy are fixtures; original values remain unknown. Success supplies neutral jackpot1/1, scalar user.iap balances or user.gold pair, user.ap or user.bp prev/cur/deadline INSIDE its resource object, and target_inst item_id/price_type/buy_cnt prev-cur. GetItemInven restores scalar global_item count rows. Independent AP/BP counters, resource balances and wallet persist together. No native nonce was recovered: separate accepted requests are distinct purchases, transport exactly-once is not promised. Native shop receipt/relaunch validation pending.

THE PUBLISHED TABLE IS NOW THE RECOVERED CAMPAIGN (added 2026-10-03): [RECOVERED] exactly the 50 stage ids of analysis/recovered-data/campaign-stages.csv (`n_01_01`..`n_05_10`, ten per area across `n_01`..`n_05`, from LEVELING.jet chunk 0 in the base APK) and nothing else. post.description: [RECOVERED] The expedition-map chest claim. Tapping a claimable chest calls `CSRSceneMStageMap::SendRewardRequest` (0xe9a168), which hands `CSRUserDB::GetCurAreaID()` and the chest index to `CSRSyncMStage::RequestReward` (0xb3bf4c); that builds a `CPVHTTPRequest::Create<..., CPVHTTPMapToEncodedURLFormTransformer<unordered_map<string,string>>>` - a URL-encoded form POST - with EXACTLY 7 entries (`unordered_map(local_118, local_d0, 7)` at ghidra-chest-01-reward-route.txt:168) and posts it to this path (0xb3c23a). THE FIELD SET IS: app_code, app_ver, market, pvid, otp, area_id, target_achieve_cnt. [RECOVERED] `target_achieve_cnt` is NOT AN INDEX: it is `std::to_string(GetRewards()[index].achieve_cnt)` (:158-160, stride 0x34), i.e. the reference value from the area's `achieve_reward[]` on /reference/GetArea. [RECOVERED] `ret_data` must be a JSON OBJECT - ReqRewardCB (0xb3c674) dispatches on `*rd` (`:586-612`, `== 1` object, `== 2` array, anything else is an error path). [RECOVERED, load-bearing] `ret_data.achieve_cnt` must EQUAL one of the area's published `achieve_reward[].achieve_cnt` values: the callback scans `GetRewards()` for that match (:526-577, :531/:566) and only then calls `SetAchieveRewardReceived(area, i)` (:570), which is what makes `found` true and hands `AchieveRewardCB` an index instead of -1 (`:1256-1263`). With -1 the callback does nothing but `Toast(); return;` (`:1776-1783`) and **the chest never reaches the `opened` sprite state**. [RECOVERED] That state matters because `SetRewardVisible(i, state)` (0xe95eb8) makes TWO of its four slots visible on `state == 1` - the `MS_RW_<L>` animation (slot +0x08) and the `MS_RW_<L>8` still (slot +0x18) - which is literally 'open and closed at the same time'; only `state == 2` clears it, and only a successful claim reaches that. [RECOVERED] `result_code` is 1 on EVERY path, refusals included: ReqRewardCB bails to `cb(-1, 0)` on any non-1 code (`:463-473`) and CPVHTTPManager::Enqueue retries - the 8x silent retry measured for /mission/Complete in analysis/testing/report-017.md. A refusal is therefore expressed by the PAYLOAD (an `achieve_cnt` that matches no published reward), never by the code. [RECOVERED] `achievement` is OMITTED, never `[]` - `:517-520` is an IS-NULL test and the branch calls `CSRAchieve::ParseAchievementsElement` (0x8481c4), a `/dailyquest/GetInstList` REQUEST builder, from inside a response callback. `free_iap`, `iap`, `supply` and `card` are omitted so their gated branches are skipped entirely. [FIXTURE] The gold amounts and the item ids come from the local chest table in src/bootstrap.ts; the item ids 912/913/914 ARE recovered CHAR_STR_RO rows ('Transcendence Ticket'), the amounts are not. Server-side bookkeeping: (area_id, achieve_cnt) is recorded on the account and persisted, so a replay is answered idempotently and pays nothing.

post.description: Consumes one persistent AP and records the requested stage as an active local battle. The handler accepts stage_id/stage/id plus optional deck_inst_id_1..4 fields and returns a fresh battle_id per fresh attempt. It replays the existing battle only within a short idempotency window (BLUSTONE_MISSION_START_IDEMPOTENCY_SECONDS, default 30, 0 disables it, 'forever' reproduces the pre-2026-10-02 unbounded behaviour), so a duplicate tap or a client transport retry does not charge AP twice while a new attempt minutes later is a genuinely new battle. [POLICY DECISION, NOT RECOVERED] The window length is a local policy: the only recovered fact is that the client can retry a request (CPVHTTPRequest::GetRetryCnt, ELF 0x151773), which is why a window exists at all. Before 2026-10-02 the guard had no age test, so a persisted battle from one early run was replayed for six consecutive device reports (report-010..report-015). Superseded battles are discarded and their AP is not refunded. This is the server-side seam for the future native battle protocol; no turn simulation, skill execution or anti-cheat is implemented.

post.description: CSRGameStage::SetArea expects an OBJECT with area, stage and achieve_reward arrays. area records define destination IDs, type, serial, level_limit and presentation strings. Type 1 is the normal expedition type (confirmed by the BT_NOMAL click handler). stage records link area_id to stage_id with a serial. TWO THINGS ON THIS ROUTE ARE EASY TO GET BACKWARDS. (1) `resource_id` is an ART name - the mission-map backdrop - and NOT an environments.csv id; see the AreaCatalog.resource_id description for the full chain. Publishing `ST001` (the stage `thumb` family) produced `[ERR] [RES] Can't find 'ST001' in ResMap.` in 5/5 r015 legs and a black map backdrop beneath a working snow layer; publishing an environment id instead would produce `Can't find '99' in ResMap.` instead. (2) `area[i].stage[]` must be NESTED inside each area record, not a sibling of `area` - that nesting is why the expedition map had no selectable stage. THE PUBLISHED CAMPAIGN (added 2026-10-03) IS THE RECOVERED ONE. [RECOVERED] Six areas are published: the origin node `n_00` plus the five expedition areas `n_01`..`n_05`, from analysis/recovered-data/campaign-stages.csv (50 stages, `n_01_01`..`n_05_10`, exactly ten per area, extracted from LEVELING.jet chunk 0 in the base APK). One monster was previously published under three keys (M001, 001, ""); because all three shared one _server, __emplace_unique_key_args kept a single node and dropped the rest, so that table could never answer a lookup for "001" or "". The published set is now derived from the same FIXTURE_MONSTER_IDS list that fills show_thumbnail AND the wave records' `ref_id` on /reference/GetTargetStageMonster, because FUN_00b4a7a8 (0xb4a7a8) builds the GetMonster request `list` from both - see that route's description. post.description: [RECOVERED] CSRSyncMStage::ReqTargetStageMonsterCB (0xb4606c) iterates ret_data and calls CSRGameMob::AddStageMonster (0xa0d194) once per top-level key, passing iteration_proxy_value::key() and the value; that key argument becomes the std::map<string, STAGE_MONSTER_LINK> key at CSRGameMob+0xc. THE KEY MUST BE THE STAGE ID, and the monster id is published alongside it. CSRMStage::MakeStageInst (0xb33f84) reads that map with GetStageMonsterLinkData(this+0x220) (0xb34b18), and this+0x220 is the scene's own stage-id string (0xb34026 -> 0xb34198 -> 0xb34686 -> 0xb34b16). On a miss GetStageMonsterLinkData (0xa0cf38) takes its `if (uVar1 == 0)` branch and returns the two fallback vectors at CSRGameMob+0x18 / +0x24, which have no writer in the library, so waves is empty; MakeStageInst then takes beq.w 0x00b34e88 at 0xb34b28, never creates the "enemy" key, and faults at 0xb3507a str r0,[r1,#0x4c] with r1 == 0. THAT is the SIGSEGV. Each value carries its wave array under `wave_list` (literal 0x01d76bd5, the only wave-array key: the load at 0xa0d1b0 is consumed solely by add r1,pc at 0xa0d1b8, and the body has exactly five basic_json::operator[] call sites with no `_id` among them; the earlier `_id` reading of the same literal slot was a resolver pairing artefact). THE WAVE ARRAY IS NESTED: `wave_list` is vector<vector<STAGE_MONSTER>>, an array of waves each holding an array of monster records. Evidence: the OUTER dereference of wave_list (bl 0x0072aff0 at 0xa0d266) is what the INNER loop iterates (bl 0x0072af38 at 0xa0d2d8), and one vector<STAGE_MONSTER> is pushed per outer element (bl 0x00a0e4ac at 0xa0d480). A FLAT array is fatal, not degraded: the inner loop then walks the monster object's own members and calls operator[] on a scalar at 0xa0d304, which nlohmann answers with a throwing type_error.305, and AddStageMonster has no handler, so both the wave push (0xa0d480) and the map emplace (0xa0d69c) are skipped and STAGE_MONSTER_LINK is never built. PER-MONSTER FIELD TYPES: `ref_id` goes through from_json<std::string> (bl 0x00728b08 at 0xa0d310) and must therefore be a non-empty JSON STRING or it throws type_error.302; `group` and `next_spawn_ms` go through a total tbb switch (subs r1,#0x3 ; cmp r1,#0x4 ; bhi -> movs r0,#0 at 0xa0d34e / 0xa0d39c) that cannot throw and returns 0 for any unhandled tag, so they must be JSON NUMBERS (next_spawn_ms is then scaled by the float constant loaded from slot 0x00a0d4f8 at 0xa0d3ec). RETRACTED 2026-10-02: the earlier claim that the ret_data key is what FUN_00b4a7a8 pushes verbatim into GET /reference/GetMonster's `list` was wrong. FUN_00b4a7a8 (0xb4a7a8) walks STAGE_MONSTER_LINK::ids FIRST, and that vector is built by AddStageMonster from the RECORD-LEVEL show_thumbnail array (literal 0x01d76bed, slot 0x00a0d874, reached only from the outer loop's exit at 0xa0d260), each element passed through from_json<std::string> (bl 0x00728b08 at 0xa0d5ac). show_thumbnail must therefore be an ARRAY OF NON-EMPTY MONSTER-ID STRINGS whose elements resolve in /reference/GetMonster. A JSON number there is not a wrong value but a wrong TYPE: the type-tag switch in AddStageMonster only iterates array and object tags, so the previous integer 1 produced an empty ids vector and GetMonster was never asked for anything resolvable. [RECOVERED] AND THERE IS A SECOND SOURCE: FUN_00b4a7a8 has a SECOND loop, over the wave vector, whose inner stride is 0x14 - exactly the 20-byte STAGE_MONSTER whose first 12 bytes are the wave's `ref_id` (00b4a864 `adds r5,#0x14`; 00b4a870 `bl 0x00a0b428 HasMonsterData`; 00b4a886 `bl 0x006d7efc` string copy) - and it appends that ref_id to the SAME list head (sp+0x24) and counter (sp+0x2c) as the ids loop. So `GET /reference/GetMonster`'s `list` is `ids` UNION {every wave record's ref_id}, and EVERY wave `ref_id` must be a published MONSTER id or CSRGameMob::GetMonsterData (0xa0b43c) misses at SRGameMob.cpp(38). This was measured: shipping the card id 001 produced the request list=["M001","001"] and the assertion followed by a fault 31-45 ms later (analysis/testing/report-014.md). The replica now ships the monster id M001 as the wave ref_id. Do NOT repair a miss by editing show_thumbnail or by publishing a monster under _server "001": the wave loop requests ref_id itself, so either would move the assertion instead of clearing it. UNRESOLVED: ref_id also reaches CSRCard::SetRefID, which wants a CARD id; that conflict is scoped, not solved, and the five SRCard.cpp(731) assertions of AGENTS.md section 11 live in the player camp (CSRMStage+0x250), not the enemy camp this change targets (CSRMStage+0x264). A/B: BLUSTONE_WAVE_SHAPE=flat restores the superseded flat array, BLUSTONE_STAGE_MONSTER_KEY=monster_id restores the pre-fix monster-id-only keying, BLUSTONE_STAGE_MONSTER_KEY=stage_id restores the superseded stage-keyed shape (the control leg of analysis/testing/report-011.md), BLUSTONE_SHOW_THUMBNAIL=scalar restores the previous integer, and BLUSTONE_WAVE_REF_ID=card restores the card wave ref_id. All five are guarded by assertions in tests/smoke.ts. [FIXTURE] The M001 ids, the card id 001 and every balance number are local fixture choices, not recovered content; enemy AI, turn order, skill execution and rewards remain incomplete.

post.description: [RECOVERED] The premium recruitment pull, reachable in game for free from the defeat screen's "Recruit New Hunter" button (analysis/research/in-game-stats.md §5.3). The client really issues `POST /shop/GachaPremium` with the 9-key set `app_code, app_ver, bonus_level, cnt, gacha_type, item_inst_id, market, otp, pvid` and `cnt: "11"` for the 10+1 button; the request builder is `CSRSyncLottery::RequestGachaPremium` (Ghidra 0xf74774, `analysis/native-network-decomp.txt:8544`), whose `_RMAssert(param_5 == 1 || param_5 == 0xb, … 0xb3)` pins `gacha_type` to {1, 11}. [RECOVERED] `ret_data` MUST be a JSON OBJECT: `CSRSyncLottery::ReqGachaPremiumCB` (0xf74fb0) reads `ret_data["card"]` at 0xf75204, iterates it calling `CSRPlayData::ParseCardInst` (0xb69598, which delegates to `CSRCard::parse` at 0x8680a4) and `CSRInventory::AddCard` (0xad9238) per element, and then hands the SAME json to the app callback as a `vector<basic_json>` - the sink in its recovered mangled signature. **The generic mock was the whole bug**: it had no `card` key, so the callback branched to 0xf654e0 before building the vector and `CSRPopUpGachaX10Result::ReqGachaPremiumCB` (0xcd7518) opened with nothing - the measured 'Response 398 B, gems stayed at 60K, no card' symptom. [RECOVERED] `cnt` MUST BE A JSON NUMBER: the read is `ldrb r1,[r0]; subs r1,#3; cmp r1,#4; bhi 0xf653d8` and only tags 3..7 reach `strtod`, so an object, an array or null takes the reject branch. [RECOVERED] each `card[]` element carries the `CSRCard::parse` instance columns (`inst_id` 0x8680be, `ref_id` 0x86810c, `lock`, `skin_*`, `weapon_*`, `armor_*`, `accessory_*`, `skill_1..5_level`, `mirage_remain_hp`) PLUS the six keys `CSRPopUpGachaX10Result::RESULT::parse` (0xcd36a8) reads with **no null guard**: `index_id`, `is_duplicate`, `inst_id` (all `strtod`), `reward.ref_id` (`from_json<std::string>`, so a STRING) and `reward.qty` (`strtod`). A missing key walks a JSON null and throws `type_error.305`. Afterwards the popup resolves the award through `CSRInventory::FindCardInstBySerial(inst_id)` -> `GetCardRefID` -> `CSRCardInfoContainer::GetCardData(ref_id)`, so both the element's `ref_id` and `reward.ref_id` must be published by `/reference/GetCard`. result.description: 0 while active; 1 for the local win result.

MissionCompleteResponse.description: result_code is 1 for EVERY outcome including a defeat: ReqCompleteCB L1133-1151 silently retries any non-1 code up to eight times and then discards the response unparsed. A loss is expressed by the payload, never by the code.

achieve.description: [RECOVERED] Newly granted flags0..2. Empty for defeat or a replay with no improvement; replays may earn missing performance conditions. Distinct from lobby stage.achieve, which is JSON-encoded array TEXT.

order.description: [RECOVERED] Three-byte flag bound from ParseMissionInfo/GetStageAchieveCnt. Index3 is out of bounds.

exp.description: Native r5 retains the EXP object: level/AP-cap pairs are nested INSIDE user.exp. Level follows the published threshold count; current fixture0/100 caps Team level at2. Native level-up popup validation remains pending.

card.description: [RECOVERED] Decimal owned serial keys with direct absolute EXP prev/cur pairs. Local policy grants published character_exp10 to up to four snapshotted participants per new matching win, including replays; no defeat/duplicate reward. Ordinary EXP caps preserve old over-cap values; unknown awakening curves stay untouched. Native EXP/result UI validation pending.

clear.description: [FIXTURE] Local echo of play_info.clear, the client's own win byte from MISSIONPLAY_INFO+0x28.

stars.description: [FIXTURE, inert] The wire carries stars in achieve[].order; this is a local mirror. The native `star`/`prev_star`/`is_first_clear` are client-derived and are deliberately NOT sent.

PreviousCur.description: [RECOVERED] {prev,cur} integer pair. prev is the value before this completion; cur is what the client stores. prev == cur means no change was applied.

MissionAchieveRewardResponse.description: result_code is 1 on EVERY path, refusals included. ReqRewardCB bails to cb(-1,0) on any non-1 code (:463-473) and the transport retries, which is the 8x silent retry storm measured for /mission/Complete. A refusal is expressed by the PAYLOAD: an `achieve_cnt` that matches no published achieve_reward entry.

achieve_cnt.description: [RECOVERED] Must equal one of this area's /reference/GetArea `achieve_reward[].achieve_cnt` values. That value is what `CSRSyncMStage::RequestReward` sent as `target_achieve_cnt`, so echoing it is what flips the chest to the `opened` sprite state - the only state in which the double-sprite artifact stops drawing.

requested_target_achieve_cnt.description: The raw form field, verbatim - it is a string on the wire.

claimed.description: false for a refusal and for an already-opened chest.

authenticated.description: false when the credential could not be resolved; the response is still result_code 1 and pays nothing.

area_achieve_cnt.description: The replica's own progress total for this area (sum of per-stage achieve over the area's links).

required_achieve_cnt.description: The threshold this chest is drawn at: GetStageCnt(area) * (index + 1).

achieve_cnt.description: [RECOVERED] GetStageCnt(area) * (index + 1). Also the exact value /mission/ReqAchieveReward must echo back.

gold.description: [FIXTURE] 300/200/100. The mechanism is recovered - ReqRewardCB applies ret_data.gold.cur only when prev != 0.

free_iap.description: [RECOVERED] key. Gated on CPVDataMgr+0x58; the replica leaves it 0 and omits the response-side twin.

iap.description: [RECOVERED] key. Gated on CPVDataMgr+0x5c; the replica leaves it 0.

card_list.description: [RECOVERED] vector<pair<string,uint32>> at ACHIEVE_REWARD+0x28. EMPTY on purpose.

id.description: [RECOVERED] The area identity. `CSRGameStage::GetAreaData` takes an area_id and `CSRUserDB::GetCurAreaID()` supplies it as `area_id` on /mission/ReqAchieveReward, so this is the value the chest claim is filed under. `area_id` is NOT published on the record itself: the recovered note that 'the identity field is area_id, not id' refers to the SRGameStage.cpp key cluster, and every link/reward record carries its own `area_id`.

type.description: 1 is normal expedition; other types pending reconstruction.

serial.description: [RECOVERED] The PER-TYPE ORDINAL at AREA_INFO+0x3c. `GetAreaData(AREA_INFO::TYPE, int)` (0x00a296f0) matches `+0x44 == type` AND `+0x3c == index` for `index in [0, GetAreaCnt(type))` and returns a shared EMPTY record on a miss, so the ordinals of one type must be a dense 0..N-1 run; `SetAreaState` then indexes the button array with it (`*(this+0x768) + area->0x3c * 8`). Ordinal 0 is the hidden origin node - `SetMarker` calls `SetVisible(button, i != 0)` (0xe74804 :337). [INFERRED key] that it is the JSON key `serial`; it is the only per-area integer in SetArea's key set that is not `level_limit` (+0x40, compared against GetUserLevel). assertAreaSerials() refuses a gap or a duplicate at boot, because either is a SILENT content loss rather than a crash.

level_limit.description: [RECOVERED] AREA_INFO+0x40 and a REAL GATE: `CSRSceneAreaSel::SetAreaState` (0xe75cdc :962-974) writes the locked sprite when `CSRPlayData::GetUserLevel() < area.level_limit`. [FIXTURE, safety-clamped to 0] the replica publishes 0 on every area because /lobby/Enter publishes no user `level`, so any ladder would gate content behind a value the server never sends - the same class of bounded-placeholder decision as the `achieve[].order` 1..3 clamp. BLUSTONE_AREA_LEVEL_LIMIT re-introduces a ladder for A/B.

resource_id.description: [RECOVERED] THE MISSION-MAP BACKDROP ART NAME. NOT AN ENVIRONMENTS.CSV ID - this is the opposite of the stage `res_prefix` trap and getting it wrong in either direction is fatal-but-silent. Evidence: `CSRGameStage::SetArea` (0xa28108, literal 0x1d7770e) is the field's only reader and SetArea's recovered 27-key set contains no environment field; the `std::map<string,ENV_INFO>` at CSRStaticData+0x150 has exactly one reader, `CSRGameBase::OnInitBackground` (0x9cbf34), and its three callers all take the key from elsewhere (`CSRGameBase::InitBackground` 0x9cbe8c reads the STAGE's `res_prefix` at stage+0x70; `CSRSceneMEpisode::InitBackground` 0xb23e80 reads a LOCAL episode COMBAT JSON, not a route; `CSRExploreMirage::InitBackground` 0x926778 is the mirage override). The consumer is `CSRSceneMStageMap::CreateArea` (0xe91f0c), whose instruction order is PA_MAP_RD_%d (0xe9205e) -> PA_MAP_SP_%d (0xe920ca) -> PA_MAP_EV_%d (0xe92136) -> PA_MAP%d (0xe921d6) -> FindByName("PA_BG") (0xe9222c) -> [load this art] -> SR_SNOW (0xe92490); PA_MAP%d and PA_BG are UI NODE names, because the recovered layout record KO/NEW/SR_MISSION/2_SR_UI_MS_ST/1_MS_ST_MAP defines 51 PA_MAP0..PA_MAP50 panels each wrapping an EMPTY <panel name="PA_BG"> plus RE_MK0..RE_MK9 marker rects and exactly one res-name (ST_SHADOW), so code fills the backdrop. The miss is an ART miss - `[ERR] [RES] Can't find 'X' in ResMap.` is CRMResMap::GetResInfo (0x01d999cb) followed by `LoadAnim2 'X' failure` and `[ERR] [LoadAnim] Cannot find the resource(X)`, then `[WRN] [OnPlay] Cannot play the node,itrdon't have A resource of image` - NOT the environment signature, which is PREFIXLESS names (_A0.._A9/_D0.._D9/_E0.._E9) and appears only at the battle. Measured in analysis/r015/logcat-all.txt: exactly ONE miss per session, ~40 s before the battle, at lines 20620/65586/109593/157904/206015, for the value "ST001" - one per AREA, not one per STAGE (the fixture publishes 17 stages), which is what identifies it as the area field rather than the stage `thumb`. [FIXTURE] the value MAP_ZONE_1 is the only MAP* pack in the recovered corpus (6129328 bytes) and is NOT proven to resolve: entry names inside these containers are not plaintext, so pack existence does not imply a resolvable entry. A value that is an environments.csv #ID or an ST<n> prefix is REFUSED AT BOOT by assertAreaBackdropArt (src/bootstrap.ts) and by tests/area-backdrop.ts.

achieve_reward.description: The area's own three chest rewards, nested - the form analysis/research/chest-rewards.md §Q2 reads from SetArea. The identical records are ALSO published at the top level; see AreaCatalog.achieve_reward for why both are sent.

stage.description: The area's own stage links, NESTED - this is the form SetArea reads. Their COUNT is S = GetStageCnt(area), the chest-label multiplier. See the top-level `stage` for the field list and the [UNKNOWN-4] note.

stage_id.description: [RECOVERED] A stage id from /reference/GetStage. Every link resolves to a published record; assertAreaLinksResolve() refuses the replica at boot otherwise, because a dangling link only costs GetStageAchieveCnt 0 - the progress total shrinks SILENTLY and the node cannot be played.

serial.description: [RECOVERED shape, [FIXTURE] values] `CSRGameStage::STAGE_LINK` is 0x1c bytes = {int32 serial; std::string id} - serial FIRST, then the id (CSRSceneMStageMap::OnInit reads `*piVar8` as the serial and `piVar8+4` as the string, and advances `piVar8 += 7`), and OnInit inserts `(serial -> GetStageAchieveCnt(id))` into an ORDERED std::map<int,int>, so the serial is an ORDERING KEY, not a flag. The replica therefore publishes 1..10 in position order - the only shape ever MEASURED to render a correct map. The recovered CSV's own serial column is 1..9,0 in EVERY area (not only n_05_10), so it is either a boss flag or an extractor artefact: [UNRESOLVED], and deliberately not published. `chest-rewards.md` Q2's 0,1,2 suggestion was NOT adopted either - IsOpened's key domain is unknown and the device has never faulted.

items.description: [RECOVERED] The area->stage links, NESTED per area (this is what the decompile shows; the sibling top-level array is kept as evidence because the chapter shield marker depends on it). Their COUNT is `S = CSRGameStage::GetStageCnt(area)`, the multiplier behind the three chest labels `S / 2S / 3S`. [UNKNOWN-4] `GetStageCnt` and `GetStageLinks` both compare the link's single string against their argument while `OnInit` feeds that same string to `GetStageAchieveCnt`, which is keyed by STAGE id - both readings cannot be true of one field, so both keys are published.

achieve_reward.description: [RECOVERED] One entry per DRAWN CHEST. `CSRSceneMStageMap::ShowReward` (0xe9413c) draws exactly three (`:2539-2572`, `:3207-3231`) - there is no data-driven count - so this array has three entries per published area and `achieve_reward[i].achieve_cnt` MUST equal `GetStageCnt(area) * (i+1)`. AN EMPTY ARRAY IS THE 'CANNOT RECEIVE THE REWARD' BUG: `CSRSyncMStage::ReqRewardCB` (0xb3c674) answers a claim by matching `ret_data.achieve_cnt` against this catalog (`:531`/`:566`) and only a match calls `SetAchieveRewardReceived` (`:570`), so with nothing to match `cb(-1, 0)` fires, `AchieveRewardCB` toasts and returns, and the chest never flips to its `opened` sprite. This array was `[]` in this replica until 2026-10-03. [RECOVERED notes are ambiguous on the nesting] AGENTS.md §11 lists achieve_reward[] at the `ret_data` level with an `area_id` field; analysis/research/chest-rewards.md §Q2 lists it as a PER-AREA member of `SetArea`. Both are published, for the same reason `stage[]` is: an extra key the parser ignores is inert, a missing key is not.

_server.description: [RECOVERED, inferred] the key AddMonster builds m_mMonsters on. Its literal 0x01d676bb is the FIRST thing AddMonster (0xa0b540) reads, and AddMonster takes no id argument, so this string - not the published object key - is what CSRGameMob::GetMonsterData looks up. Must be non-empty and must equal the ids published in the show_thumbnail array of /reference/GetTargetStageMonster.

wave_list.description: [RECOVERED] THE WAVE ARRAY, and it is TWO DEEP. `wave_list` is the only wave-array key AddStageMonster (0xa0d194) reads (literal 0x01d76bd5; the OUTER dereference at 0xa0d266 is what the INNER loop at 0xa0d2d8 iterates, and one vector<STAGE_MONSTER> is pushed per outer element at 0xa0d480). Each outer element is one WAVE and each inner element is one MONSTER RECORD. MUST BE NON-EMPTY at both levels: an empty outer array makes MakeStageInst skip the writer at 0xb34b28 and fault at 0xb3507a; an empty wave pushes no ACTOR_INFO. A FLAT array is fatal - the inner loop would walk the monster object's own members and call operator[] on a scalar at 0xa0d304, which throws type_error.305. Control leg: BLUSTONE_WAVE_SHAPE=flat.

_id.description: Inert alias of `wave_list`. `_id` exists in .rodata tail-merged four bytes earlier (0x1d76bd1) and tools/resolve-literals-offline.py reports it, but that is a pairing artefact: the load at 0xa0d1b0 is consumed only by add r1,pc at 0xa0d1b8 (yielding `wave_list`), and the body has exactly five basic_json::operator[] call sites (0xa0d1ce, 0xa0d304, 0xa0d34a, 0xa0d398, 0xa0d512) with no `_id` among them. Published as an alias so the unused key cannot drift.

show_thumbnail.description: [RECOVERED] array of monster-id strings, read at RECORD level after the wave loop (operator[] at 0xa0d512, reached only from the outer loop's exit at 0xa0d260) with from_json<std::string> per element (0xa0d5ac). The resulting vector is STAGE_MONSTER_LINK::ids, which FUN_00b4a7a8 walks to build GET /reference/GetMonster's `list` - it is ONE of the two sources of that list; the other is every wave record's `ref_id`. Every element must resolve against /reference/GetMonster's published `_server` values. A non-array value yields an EMPTY ids vector (the type-tag switch only opens an iteration window for array and object tags). Control leg: BLUSTONE_SHOW_THUMBNAIL=scalar.

ref_id.description: [RECOVERED] INERT at record level: all four wave-keyed operator[] sites in AddStageMonster target the INNER dereference at 0xa0d2e8, so nothing reads this one. It mirrors the first wave record's ref_id so the response cannot be self-contradictory; asserted equal in tests/smoke.ts.

[RECOVERED] read by operator[] at 0xa0d304 and converted with from_json<std::string> (bl 0x00728b08 at 0xa0d310), which THROWS type_error.302 on any other JSON type. Non-empty string: it becomes the 12-byte ref_id of the 20-byte STAGE_MONSTER (stride 0x14 at 0xa0d410). [RECOVERED] IT MUST NAME A MONSTER, NOT A CARD. FUN_00b4a7a8 (0xb4a7a8) builds GET /reference/GetMonster's `list` in two loops that share one list head (sp+0x24): over STAGE_MONSTER_LINK::ids at stride 0x0c, and over the wave vector at inner stride 0x14 - which lands exactly on this string (00b4a870 HasMonsterData, 00b4a886 string copy). `list` is therefore `ids` UNION {every wave ref_id}, and CSRGameMob::GetMonsterData (0xa0b43c) resolves it with std::map<string,INFO>::find on `_server`, asserting at SRGameMob.cpp(38) when it is not published by /reference/GetMonster. Shipping the card id produced the measured list=["M001","001"] and that assertion (analysis/testing/report-014.md). [FIXTURE] the value M001, from FIXTURE_WAVE_REF_ID = FIXTURE_MONSTER_IDS[0]. [UNRESOLVED] this same string also reaches CSRCard::SetRefID, which wants a CARD id; that conflict is scoped, not solved (AGENTS.md section 11), and the player-camp SRCard.cpp(731) assertions are a separate defect. Control leg: BLUSTONE_WAVE_REF_ID=card.

group.description: [RECOVERED] read by a total tbb switch at 0xa0d34e (subs r1,#0x3 ; cmp r1,#0x4 ; bhi -> movs r0,#0) which accepts number, numeric string and bool and returns 0 for every other tag. Cannot throw.

next_spawn_ms.description: [RECOVERED] read by the same total switch at 0xa0d39c, then scaled by the float constant loaded from slot 0x00a0d4f8 at 0xa0d3ec (vmul.f32). Cannot throw.

show_thumbnail.description: [RECOVERED] INERT on a monster record: AddStageMonster reads show_thumbnail at RECORD level only (0xa0d512), never per monster. Carried because AddStageMonster is the only reader of this record.

StageReference.description: Partial native-parser reconstruction; no production stage records recovered. Other observed keys include ap_cost, gold, character_exp, group_exp, enemy_atk_per, enemy_hp_per, power, title, desc, thumb, story_id, begin_dialog_id, end_dialog_id and achieve_condition. Types and relationships beyond the fields below remain to be validated.

id.description: Compatibility/debug stage identifier; must equal stage_id.

stage_id.description: Native CSRGameStage lookup key and the identifier sent to mission-start APIs.

res_prefix.description: [RECOVERED] THE ENVIRONMENT SELECTOR, not an art name. CSRGameBase::InitBackground (0x9cbe8c) reads this field (stage+0x70) and hands it to OnInitBackground (0x9cbf34), which uses it as a std::map<string,CSRStaticData::ENV_INFO> key against CSRStaticData+0x150 - populated by CSRStaticData::LoadEnv (0xf3bab0) from environments.csv. The lookup does NOT test end(), so an unresolvable value reads the tree end-node, ENV_INFO.PreFix formats as "" and every scrolling background layer name becomes prefixless, leaving CSRGameScrollBGDraw::Load with no attached children and faulting CSRGameScrollBGDraw::OnUpdate at ELF 0x9aebd7. Valid values are the #ID column of analysis/recovered-data/environments.csv: 0-19, 99, 100, 200, 502-537, 801, 900-907, 998. The asset namespace is different (the row's PreFix is STI000/STI099/STI900, the ST*.jet family with an I inserted), so an ST001-shaped value is never valid here. [FIXTURE] this replica publishes "99".

achieve_condition.description: JSON-encoded array of achievement-condition records, NOT an embedded array.

StageCatalog.description: The native CSRGameStage::SetStage response wrapper. The stage array is required; returning a bare array leaves the local stage table empty and prevents mission start.

target_pvid.description: Blocked account identifier; replica accepts positive safe integers.

target_nickname.description: Display name resolved from the established local account.

CardInstance.description: Partial recovered instance schema. Additional equipment, skill, awakening and skin fields are supplied by the provisional fixture in src/bootstrap.ts; their full semantics remain under reconstruction.

inst_id.description: Owned instance identifier; used by decks and leader selection.

ref_id.description: Exact base.id of a loaded CardReference; never empty.

rank.description: Must have a corresponding reference stat row.

exp.description: Accumulated experience; level tables still need reconstruction.

res_prefix.description: Client asset prefix; provisional fixture value not yet validated in-game.

items.description: Rank-specific stats. Native floating_point parser expects hp/atk/def/spd and related numeric stats encoded as strings, not JSON numbers.

GachaPullAward.description: [RECOVERED] One `ret_data.card[]` element. The first block is the `CSRCard::parse` instance column set (Ghidra 0x8680a4) - byte-identical to a `/lobby/GetCardInven` row, because `CSRPlayData::ParseCardInst` (0xb69598) is the same parser both routes feed. The second block is the six keys `CSRPopUpGachaX10Result::RESULT::parse` (0xcd36a8) reads WITHOUT a null guard, so every one is mandatory; omitting any of them walks a JSON null and throws `type_error.305`. [FIXTURE] `rank`/`exp`/gear levels and `is_duplicate`.

inst_id.description: [RECOVERED] Number. Read with strtod, then used by `CSRInventory::FindCardInstBySerial` - so it must be a serial the client actually holds, which it does because the sync callback has just added this same element.

ref_id.description: [RECOVERED] The card id. Must be non-empty (`CSRCard::SetRefID` asserts `sRefID.length() > 0`, SRCard.cpp:731) and must resolve in `/reference/GetCard`.

index_id.description: [RECOVERED] Number (strtod at 0xcd36d2). Position of this draw in the result grid.

is_duplicate.description: [RECOVERED] Number (strtod at 0xcd3724). [LOCAL POLICY] 1 if that reference was previously acquired, including earlier draws in this request; collection history survives consumption.

reward.description: [RECOVERED] Object. `ref_id` is read with `from_json<std::string>` (0x718b08) so it MUST be a JSON string, not a number.

GachaPremiumResponse.description: [RECOVERED] `ret_data` of `POST /shop/GachaPremium`. `achievement`, `consumed_inst_list`, `point`, `mileage_action`, `before_point` and `after_point` are deliberately ABSENT, not empty: every one of them is reached only after an explicit null test in `CSRSyncLottery::ReqGachaPremiumCB` (0xf74fb0), so an omitted key is the smallest safe form and an empty `[]` is not.

cnt.description: [RECOVERED] Number of awards. MUST be a JSON number: the read is `ldrb; subs #3; cmp #4; bhi <reject>` and only value tags 3..7 reach `strtod`. 0 means the pull was refused for currency.

card.description: [RECOVERED] cnt1 requires ONE OBJECT: native parses whole card, not array[0]. cnt>1 requires an array. cnt0 uses null to skip the cnt<=1 parser. Sending an array for single/zero results parses an empty ref_id and crashes IsTrainingCard despite a valid reference map. Callback always receives a vector assembled by the requester.

user.description: [RECOVERED] Optional; the whole block is null-guarded at 0xf750c0. Published only so the currency readout moves after a pull.

error_code.description: [FIXTURE] Local-only breadcrumb (`GACHA_FUND_SHORT`). NOT read by any client parser - it exists so a tester reading the wire can tell a refusal from a success. It is why a refusal still answers `result_code: 1`.

GenericRequest.description: Opaque request object. Exact fields are route-specific and generally not yet confirmed.

ret_data.description: Redacted local fixture data; no recovered scalar reward values.

result_code.description: Application result code. Native ParseLauncherResp maps 1 to success; 0 is not the launcher success value.

ret_data.description: Route-specific JSON payload: an object for account replies, an array for many reference/inventory replies. See each operation's narrowed schema.

data.description: Compatibility alias of ret_data; has the same JSON value and type.

url_key.description: Application reference used by the native launcher; `_SR` is the recovered Blustone app code.

ServerRecord.description: Native app-server record. In the local replica, state 2 is the tested online path and state 1 reproduces the maintenance-WebView branch; the value is controlled by BLUSTONE_LAUNCHER_STATE.

state.description: Launcher/server state: 2 is the current online compatibility value; 1 is the maintenance branch used for reproduction.

AppServerName.description: Native app-server display record parsed from app_srv_name_list.

BaseInfo.description: Launcher configuration returned both as ret_data/data and as top-level compatibility fields by the local server.

auto_login.description: Native resume path is enabled by default; set BLUSTONE_AUTO_LOGIN=0 to force the manual title/login UI.

state.description: Launcher state: 2 is the tested online path; 1 is the maintenance branch.

otp.description: Account session token required before the client accepts server_url. Subsequent native reference/lobby forms carry this field. Different from PV-AccessToken.

vs_token.description: Persistent account credential returned by the WebView/SNS login and checked by /v2/account/Login. Guest resume may omit it.

sns_list.description: Native auto-login identity map; key 0 is the email identity when present.

nickname_confirm.description: Native login parser flag; 1 means the generated local nickname is already confirmed.

begin_utc.description: Account registration time in Unix seconds.
